title: The Scholar's True Mother Tongue (MR)
summary: A brilliant visiting polyglot challenges the court of Agra to discover his native language. Birbal uses an unexpected splash of cold water to reveal the truth. [MR]
full_text:
A renowned scholar named Pandit Ramdas arrived in Agra from the southern provinces. He was an astonishing linguist who had studied in temples and universities across Asia. He spoke Sanskrit, Persian, Arabic, Turkish, Telugu, Tamil, Marathi, and Bengali with flawless grammar and authentic native accents.

Standing before Emperor Akbar in the Diwan-i-Khas, Ramdas delivered a greeting in five different languages, switching between them with breathtaking ease. He then issued a challenge:

'Your Majesty, I have debated scholars across Hindustan, and not a single soul has been able to identify which language is my true mother tongue! I challenge your Navratnas: determine my native language within twenty-four hours, or acknowledge that my learning surpasses all the ministers of Agra!'

Akbar summoned his linguists and courtiers. For six hours, they engaged Ramdas in discussion. He quoted Kalidasa like a scholar from Ujjain, Firdausi like an archivist from Shiraz, and Tiruvalluvar like a poet from Madurai. By sunset, the imperial scholars were completely defeated.

Akbar turned to Birbal: 'Can you uncover his mother tongue?'

'Allow me until tomorrow morning, Sire,' Birbal replied with a calm smile.

That night, Ramdas was lodged in a luxurious guest suite in the palace gardens. Around midnight, after the scholar had fallen into a deep, peaceful sleep, Birbal slipped into the bedroom carrying a brass pitcher filled with icy cold water.

Birbal crept quietly to the bedside, drew back his arm, and splashed the freezing water directly onto the sleeping scholar's face!

Shocked out of deep slumber, gasping and shivering, Ramdas leaped to his feet in the dark and screamed at the top of his lungs:

'Arey! Yevaru ra meeru? Enduku ila neellu posaaru? Pichhodlaaga unnaru!' (Hey! Who are you people? Why did you pour water on me? Have you gone mad?)

Birbal stepped back, bowed politely with a smile, and whispered: 'Good night, noble Panditji. Sleep well.'

The next morning, Ramdas stood before Akbar's throne: 'Has anyone discovered my native tongue?'

Birbal stepped forward: 'Your native mother tongue is Telugu, from the fertile delta of the Godavari!'

Ramdas gasped in astonishment. He bowed low to the marble floor: 'It is true! Telugu is the language my mother spoke to me in my cradle! But how did you discover it when I spoke only refined Persian and Sanskrit in this hall?'

Birbal explained: 'A scholar can master many languages when his intellect is alert and calculating. But when a man is startled awake in sudden shock or pain, all masks fall away, and the soul cries out in its true mother tongue!'

Akbar and the court applauded Birbal's brilliant practical psychology.
